what_this_is: economic research. The world model's own states, the structure and evidence state of two transmission chains, the distribution of one employer's payroll by county of residence, the household-buffer components and their refusals, and regional market structure.
what_this_is_not: it carries no opportunity economics, no financial assumption, no portfolio construction, no marketed asset and no asking price. Those are INTERNAL under §10, are held outside every published artefact, and are not deployed.

readings.claim: This region is one federal appropriation with a county attached.
readings.what_it_says: One employer paid $1,853m of salary across six named counties. $819m of it — 40.1% — accrues to residents of Los Alamos County, and 50.7% to residents of other named counties.
readings.what_works_against_it: $187m, 9.2% of salaries, is unattributed in the operator's own table and the report does not explain it. It is counted as neither retained nor exported.

readings.claim: Residence sorts by earnings, so the county retains the top of one employer's distribution and exports the rest.
readings.what_it_says: A laboratory employee living in Los Alamos earns $151,611 on average; one living in Rio Arriba earns $92,548. A 64% spread for one employer in one year.
readings.what_works_against_it: the two figures come from two sources reporting the same FY2025 payroll — salaries from the operator's own page, employee counts from a newspaper's reading of the same report. R-08 returns NOT_EVALUATED on the ratio because the repository holds no indicator_id for an operator-published figure, so the kernel declines to certify rather than passing.

readings.claim: A world rate change can be carried to the 30-year mortgage rate and cannot be carried into this region.
readings.what_it_says: +100bp of policy lands as +0.10 to +0.37 percentage points on the 30-year mortgage rate, three steps out. The next step requires regional construction and conduit terms, and the world model records that parameter as UNKNOWN.
readings.what_works_against_it: the chain is supported again on the far side of the break. Both ends are measured and the magnitude still cannot cross, which is the condition most likely to tempt a reader into joining them.

readings.claim: A published 10% price advantage exists for regional suppliers and is observed to fail.
readings.what_it_says: On competitive acquisitions over $100,000 a 10% adjustment factor is added to the evaluated price of any bidder that is not a Northern New Mexico small business. Four of the five small-business subcontractors the cleanup contractor names are headquartered outside New Mexico.
readings.what_works_against_it: the named awards are nuclear-qualified specialities with a thin national supplier base, so the divergence may be specialism rather than regional capability failure. Not excluded by any evidence held.

readings.claim: Household economic security cannot be reported for this region, and the reason is not caution.
readings.what_it_says: The buffer is labelled INCOMPLETE_HOUSEHOLD_RESOURCE_VIEW with no score. Two of its five components are partially measured and three are not measured at all.
readings.what_works_against_it: no score. Collapsing five components of which three are unmeasured would present absence as a value.

income_by_residence.caveat: $187m (9.2%) is unattributed in the source and is not shown.

salary_per_employee.caveat: R-08 returns NOT_EVALUATED on this ratio: both inputs describe one payroll and one year, and the kernel holds no indicator_id for an operator-published figure, so it declines to certify rather than passing.

chains.title: Global financing conditions -> Northern New Mexico housing feasibility
chains.support_shape_means: both ends are supported and the magnitude cannot cross. This is worse than it looks: it means the model can measure the cause and measure the consequence and still not relate them, so a reader who sees both ends will be tempted to join them and must not
chains.rival: TCR02 -- construction input costs rather than financing cost. The same per-unit figure of roughly $500,000 appears in a 60-key hotel project on a different site with a different capital structure, which is consistent with a cost driver that is not financing. NOT EXCLUDED, and no construction cost index for the county was obtained.

the full cost is debt-financed (OBSERVED for this project: the structure states it eliminates developer equity)
operating expense fits inside $95 to $201 per unit per month at the favourable corners (UNKNOWN, and implausible)
the 380 units lease at the restricted rents (UNKNOWN)
chains.opportunity_or_threat: BOTH, and they are not symmetric. The THREAT is that every housing project in this county needs gap capital because rents do not carry cost, so a rate rise removes projects rather than repricing them -- which is what the declared identity means by 'the marginal project that becomes infeasible'. The OPPORTUNITY is subordinate or gap capital, and it exists only if some layer in a real stack prices between the public senior and an equity return. ONE DOCUMENT DECIDES WHICH.

claims.claim: A 100 basis point rise in the policy rate lands as +0.10 to +0.37 percentage points on the 30-year mortgage rate, three steps out, with a three-month lag.
claims.source: WORLD_MODEL_V0_5 §V, path QP-RATES, 3 of 3 steps, PLAUSIBLY_TRANSPORTABLE. Three time-series associations composed under a monotonicity guard.

claims.claim: A 10% rise in Brent lands as +0.56% to +1.61% on truckload freight PPI, two steps out, with a six-month lag.
The world model holds ZERO identified causal estimates of anything. All nine of its quantified relationships are time-series associations over US aggregates.
claims.source: WORLD_MODEL_V0_5 §AD, the quantification bottleneck verdict. Not determinable as structural or cyclical because an association over an aggregate does not separate the two -- that separation is exactly what identification would buy.

claims.claim: Quantification is NOT the binding constraint on this model. Nine new estimates left every configuration pair indistinguishable, every circuit state unchanged, every historical episode verdict unchanged and every loop classification unchanged. One of nine changed a conclusion.
claims.source: WORLD_MODEL_V0_5 §A and §AD. A tested and rejected hypothesis, not an opinion. Not a structural/cyclical question at all -- it is a property of the model.

claims.claim: Quantitatively traversable circuits: zero. Two are partially quantified, one refuses at a named step, nine are not quantified. 58 of 95 edges are magnitude-unknown.
A rate rise is structurally distinguishable from a credit contraction: there is no route from the policy rate to small-firm credit TIGHTENING, and there is one to small-firm credit DEMAND.
claims.source: WORLD_MODEL_V0_5 §A, via WR106. Structural because it is a property of the represented topology, not of a current reading.

claims.claim: Where value is created and where capital moves cannot be answered by this model. The capital allocation step is a decision among seven represented branches with no probability attached to any, and national firm finance and regional retention are not joined anywhere.
claims.source: WORLD_MODEL_V0_5 §O. The retention share is computable (median about 0.40 since 2000, IQR 0.35-0.50) and was REFUSED as a behavioural parameter, because assigning an accounting decomposition to a behavioural edge would change what it means.

claims.claim: Sustained federal nuclear-security appropriation is the dominant world force acting on this region, and it is a policy quantity rather than a market one.
claims.source: R3.8 S-01, S-03: a $5.28bn budget rising from $5.24bn, attributed by the operator's director to sustained geopolitical tensions and bipartisan support for the national security mission.

claims.claim: Over five to twenty years the region's exposure is to appropriation policy rather than to the business cycle, so the usual cyclical reasoning is the wrong frame for it.
claims.antecedent: IF the appropriation remains the dominant external flow, which is true today at $5.28bn against the next largest identified external flow of about $300m in regional film production

claims.claim: No appropriation forecast is held and none is produced. A twenty-year view of this region is a view about one legislature's choices.
claims.source: nothing in the world model or the R3 line forecasts an appropriation, and the model holds no political-economy object at all.

world.explains_well: the TOPOLOGY of transmission: which routes exist, which do not, and where a magnitude would have to attach. That is why it can state that a rate rise and a credit contraction are different objects, and why it refuses to compose two true numbers across a seam it cannot join.
world.cannot_explain: magnitude with identification, and therefore almost everything a forecast would need. It holds no identified causal estimate, no probability on any allocation branch, and no political object -- while the force that dominates this particular region is a political one.
world.honest_frame: Dula's world model is a map of mechanisms with very few measured distances. Used as a map it is good: it tells you which way a change can travel and where the road ends. Used as a forecast it would be fiction, and its own v0.5 verdict says so more sharply than any outside critic would.

markets.name: Nuclear-security research operations and its supply chain

markets.who_produces_it: Triad National Security LLC (operator, 16,487 regular employees and 1,378 contractors) and N3B Los Alamos (legacy cleanup)
markets.who_buys_it: the National Nuclear Security Administration and DOE Environmental Management. ONE BUYER, federally appropriated.
markets.where_the_customers_are: Washington. The customer is not regional and is not a market in any price-discovering sense.
markets.where_the_suppliers_are: about half of procurement is in New Mexico; the one source naming small-business subcontractors names four of five outside the state
markets.inputs_required: nuclear-qualified construction and services, radiological control labour, equipment, IT, commodities

discontinuity.observed: laboratory-wide procurement fell $700m, or 30.4%, from FY2023 to FY2025, while the budget ROSE from $5.24bn to $5.28bn.
discontinuity.r32_rule_applied: do not interpret the movement before finding its cause.
discontinuity.cause: the operator's director states that from 2024 the laboratory began extending one-year contracts to two and three years, and THE FULL VALUE OF EACH MULTIYEAR CONTRACT IS RECORDED IN THE YEAR IT IS AWARDED. Especially common in construction.
discontinuity.who_says_so: Thom Mason, laboratory director, quoted in the Santa Fe New Mexican (S-03). This is the MEASURED PARTY explaining its own series, which is evidence and not proof.
discontinuity.independent_comment: a UNM finance professor called the decline 'a little bit disappointing' and said worry would be premature unless it persisted several years: 'procurement numbers do tend to be lumpy.'
discontinuity.the_consequence_that_matters: UNDER AWARD-YEAR ACCOUNTING THE SERIES RECORDS AWARD EVENTS, NOT ANNUAL PURCHASING. So $752.5m is not FY2025's purchasable demand, and neither is any other single year's figure. ANY SUPPLIER THESIS SIZED OFF ONE YEAR OF THIS SERIES IS SIZING A BOOKKEEPING CONVENTION.
discontinuity.this_is_the_third_time: R3.2 found the FY2019 'leakage' trend was a prime contractor re-registering from New Mexico to Ohio. R3.6 found a BDS county employment break that would have reported 284% growth that never happened. Now an award-year accounting change. Three for three: every large movement in a published series examined in this programme has had a reporting cause.

preference.rule: a 10% adjustment factor is ADDED to the evaluated total price of any offeror that is NOT a Northern New Mexico small business concern, on competitive acquisitions over $100,000.
preference.qualification_bar: a small business with an operative business location in Northern New Mexico using Northern New Mexico labour; the representations form asks for three or more FTE of which 51% reside in the region, plus a local facility.
preference.plus: the eight regional Pueblos, with a separate preference for the Triad Pueblo business alliance (San Ildefonso, Ohkay Owingeh, Acoma).
preference.why_this_matters: it is a QUANTIFIED, PUBLISHED competitive advantage with a low qualification bar -- three employees and a local facility. R3.7 treated regional supplier development as an unsized signal. The advantage is 10 percentage points of evaluated price.
preference.what_it_is_not: a set-aside. It changes evaluated price, not award, and no published figure states how many awards it has decided.

reframing.observation: N3B awarded more than 80% of nearly $290m to small businesses. Of the five small-business awardees it names, FOUR ARE HEADQUARTERED OUTSIDE NEW MEXICO -- Nome Alaska, Chandler Arizona, Knoxville Tennessee, and one unstated.
reframing.inference: SMALL-BUSINESS STATUS AND REGIONAL LOCATION ARE DIFFERENT THINGS, and in the one place the data names firms, they diverge sharply. A high small-business percentage is not evidence of regional capture.
reframing.what_this_implies_for_the_opportunity: the binding constraint on regional supplier participation is CAPABILITY AND QUALIFICATION, not preference. The preference already exists and is priced at 10%; out-of-state small firms are winning anyway. Adding preference would not change it; building qualified regional capacity might.
reframing.rival: N3B operates under a different contract with different preference terms from the operator's. Its named awards are radiological control and canyon soil remediation -- nuclear-qualified specialities with a thin national supplier base. The divergence may be specialism, not a general regional failure. NOT EXCLUDED.

named_from_evidence: environmental remediation and canyon soil investigation

workflow.title: How financing conditions reach Northern New Mexico housing
workflow.why_this_one: it is the only chain in the model with evidence at both ends and a named, single missing parameter in the middle, and the only opportunity that reached a feasibility answer. Every other candidate stops earlier.

steps.question: What is the world doing that could reach this region?
steps.plain: When the policy rate rises by one percentage point, the thirty-year mortgage rate rises by roughly a tenth to four tenths of a point, about three months later. That is the furthest Dula can follow a rate change with a measured size on every step.

figures.label: pass-through of a 100bp policy rise
figures.unit: percentage points on the 30-year mortgage rate

steps.caveat: three time-series associations composed under a monotonicity guard. The interval is wide on purpose and is a minimum guard, not a correct treatment of dependence between the steps.

steps.question: Does that reach a developer in Los Alamos?
steps.plain: No, and this is the single most consequential gap in the regional model. A thirty-year residential mortgage rate is not what a housing project borrows at. Projects here borrow through tax-exempt conduit bonds and construction facilities, and no source Dula holds reports what those actually cost in Northern New Mexico. So the model can watch the world rate move and cannot say what it does to a project.
steps.what_it_costs_the_reader: every figure downstream of this point rests on an ASSUMED cost of capital. The feasibility answer below is computed at 4% and 5% because the real number is not published anywhere Dula can reach.
steps.caveat: the world model named this parameter as the blocker before any of the market research existed, and the market research arrived at the same gap from the opposite direction.

next.evidence_needed: the coupon and term on one real local housing bond
next.where_it_may_come_from: the Coyote Mesa bond ordinance, a public county council document, or any comparable New Mexico conduit issue
next.what_it_would_enable: replacing the assumed 4-5% band with an observed rate, which turns the feasibility answer below from an argument into an underwriting — and would be the first time a world rate change could be carried into a project in this region

steps.question: What does it cost to build here, and can rent carry it?
steps.plain: A workforce apartment in Los Alamos County costs about $503,000 to $526,000 to build, all in. The median existing home in the same county is worth $495,800. It costs roughly the price of a house to build an apartment, and that single comparison explains everything about how these projects are financed.
steps.caveat: the per-unit figure is all-in — land treatment, infrastructure, financing and issuance — and is not a builder's hard cost.

steps.question: Does the restricted rent cover the debt?
steps.plain: Barely, or not at all, depending on the rate nobody has published. At a 4% coupon the rent ceiling leaves $95 to $201 a month per unit after debt service; at 5% it is $113 to $234 a month SHORT. The headroom at the favourable corners then has to pay for management, maintenance, insurance, reserves and vacancy — and nothing plausible fits in $201 a month.

figures.label: per-unit debt service
figures.source: computed; rate and term are declared assumptions

steps.caveat: the rate and the 35-year term are ASSUMPTIONS, not observations, because of the hinge at step 2. No operating-expense figure for comparable New Mexico multifamily was obtained, so the headroom cannot be tested against a real budget.

next.evidence_needed: an operating-expense figure per unit per month for comparable New Mexico multifamily
next.where_it_may_come_from: an MFA-financed property's audited operating statement, or a state housing agency underwriting standard
next.what_it_would_enable: net operating income, and therefore cash flow, valuation and any return expectation — three of the fifteen financial terms are blocked by this one figure

workflow.what_the_reader_should_conclude: Workforce housing in Los Alamos is needed, is being built, and cannot be financed on its rents. The project going ahead does so with no developer equity, tax-exempt conduit debt, a county purchase of deed restrictions and a state predevelopment grant, with the residual going to the county. A structure built to eliminate equity is the market stating that equity cannot be paid.
workflow.what_the_reader_should_not_conclude: that the figures at step 4 are an underwriting. Two of the three inputs are assumptions forced by the gap at step 2, and the term that carries the economic meaning — the MARGINAL project, the one that does not go ahead — is unobserved. Every project anyone can see is one that proceeded.

interactive.title: What happens if construction financing costs change

opportunity_link.name: Subordinate and gap capital for workforce housing
opportunity_link.what_the_table_shows: the principal a restricted rent can actually carry at each coupon, and therefore how much of the unit cost it cannot. That remainder is the gap R1 exists to fill.
opportunity_link.why_this_is_the_link: the regional financing mechanism and the candidate are the same arithmetic seen from two ends. A coupon rise does not make this opportunity more attractive -- it makes it LARGER AND HARDER, because the gap grows while the evidence that anything can be charged for filling it does not.
opportunity_link.what_it_still_does_not_establish: whether any coupon is payable on that subordinate layer. The gap is computable; the price of filling it is not, and that single unknown is what keeps R1 at feasibility rather than underwriting.

interactive.model: r38_feasibility._annuity, the same function behind the static four corners
interactive.equation: level annual payment = P × r / (1 − (1+r)^−n), divided by twelve

adjustable.name: assumed construction / conduit coupon
adjustable.why_adjustable: because the model does not hold it. CONSTRUCTION_LOAN_TERMS_NNM is UNKNOWN, so every figure downstream of it is conditional on a number the analyst chooses rather than one Dula observed.
adjustable.warning: MOVING THIS SLIDER DOES NOT TELL YOU WHAT LENDERS CHARGE. It tells you what the project's arithmetic does IF the coupon were that. No source Dula holds reports actual Northern New Mexico construction or conduit terms, and a number you picked is not a market quote.

fixed_inputs.name: term
fixed_inputs.note: a conventional long-dated tax-exempt housing bond term. The actual term is not published.

fixed_inputs.name: share debt-financed
fixed_inputs.note: not a free assumption: the developer's own page states the structure eliminates developer equity.

fixed_inputs.name: 80%-of-AMI gross housing ceiling
fixed_inputs.note: HUD 2024 four-person 80% limit of $97,800 × 30% ÷ 12. FY2026 limits were not confirmed.

operating_model.title: What the restricted rent can carry once the project has to be operated
operating_model.defaults_are_zero: the three unknown lines default to ZERO. At zero this statement reproduces the published four corners exactly, which is the point: the published result is a FLOOR, and every real value for these lines makes it worse.

adjustable_unknowns.name: tenant-paid utility allowance
adjustable_unknowns.why: HUD's 80% limit is a GROSS housing cost: rent plus tenant-paid utilities. The project collects the ceiling MINUS this allowance, so a non-zero value lowers every rent figure in the model.
adjustable_unknowns.obtain_from: the utility allowance schedule published by the public housing authority for Los Alamos County, or the schedule in the project's own regulatory agreement.
adjustable_unknowns.range_basis: EXPLORATION BOUNDS, NOT AN ESTIMATE. Dula holds no utility allowance schedule for this county and does not guess one.

adjustable_unknowns.name: vacancy and collection loss
adjustable_unknowns.why: rent is collected on occupied units. Absorption of 380 units in a county of this size is the question nobody retrieved has answered.
adjustable_unknowns.obtain_from: the project's lease-up reporting to the county, or a Los Alamos / Santa Fe multifamily vacancy series.

adjustable_unknowns.name: operating expenses
adjustable_unknowns.why: management, maintenance, insurance, reserves and any payment in lieu of property tax. r38_feasibility excludes all of it and records that NO New Mexico multifamily operating-expense figure was obtained.
adjustable_unknowns.obtain_from: the operating pro forma in the bond Official Statement, or New Mexico Mortgage Finance Authority owner-reported operating data for comparable restricted properties.
adjustable_unknowns.range_basis: EXPLORATION BOUNDS, NOT AN ESTIMATE. No figure is held, so no sensitivity range here is defensible and none is offered.

the_inversion.what_it_is: the largest per-unit monthly operating budget consistent with paying debt service out of the restricted rent -- the ceiling less debt service. It needs NO estimate of operating cost, because it is the bound an estimate would have to fit inside.
the_inversion.why_it_is_the_honest_form: an invented operating expense would produce a precise NOI and a precise DSCR, both fictional. The bound is arithmetic on observed cost and a published rent limit, and a reader can test it against any operating budget they already know.

no_coverage_ratio.what_is_not_computed: a debt service coverage ratio, at any rate
no_coverage_ratio.why: a coverage ratio is net operating income over debt service. CASH_FLOW is NOT_ESTABLISHED in the financial lens because no operating expense for comparable New Mexico multifamily is held, so there is no numerator. A ratio computed with operating expenses set to zero is the rent ceiling divided by debt service wearing a finance word, and it would read as an underwriting result to anyone who skipped the label.
no_coverage_ratio.what_replaces_it: the bound: the largest operating budget the restricted rent leaves room for. It needs no numerator, because it IS the numerator's upper limit.

breakeven.means: the coupon at which the 80%-of-AMI ceiling exactly covers debt service and nothing remains for any operating cost. Above it the project cannot service its debt from restricted rent at all.
breakeven.solved_how: bisection on the same annuity function, to three decimals

what_changes_when_you_move_it: per-unit monthly debt service, on both cost estimates
the headroom against the 80%-of-AMI ceiling, and its sign
whether the project clears its debt from restricted rent at all
how much subordinate or grant capital per unit would be needed to close the gap
what_does_not_change: the all-in cost per unit — it is observed, and financing cost is not construction cost
the rent ceiling — it is set by the income distribution of the county and a HUD formula, not by the lender
the capital structure — no developer equity, whatever the coupon
who takes the residual — the county, by the terms of the structure

what_cannot_be_completed.blocked_by: no operating-expense figure for comparable New Mexico multifamily
what_cannot_be_completed.consequence: headroom is the closest available proxy and it is NOT NOI: it is what is left before any operating cost, not after.

DSCR = NOI / debt service. The denominator moves with this slider and the numerator does not exist, so no coverage ratio is computed at any rate. Dividing the ceiling by debt service would LOOK like a DSCR and would be a rent-to-debt ratio.
there is no equity position to size or to return. This is not a missing figure; it is an absent instrument.
this is the parameter the slider stands in for. The slider explores consequences; it does not discover the rate.
